1.explanation:
• createConfig in devtools-entry.js sets screenEmulation.disabled = true for all DevTools runs. That flag is passed through to Lighthouse, causing getEmulationDescriptions to think no emulation was applied even though DevTools had already emulated the viewport.  
• emulate in core/lib/emulation.js checks settings.screenEmulation.disabled and, when true, skips calling Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride and related commands. This reinforces the “no emulation” state internally.  
Together these two functions are responsible for both disabling real viewport emulation in the protocol and misreporting the emulation status in the DevTools UI.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse from within DevTools on a mobile device emulation, the summary bar in the Lighthouse panel still reads “No emulation with Lighthouse” (see screenshot). The root cause is that devtools-entry.js’s createConfig call force-disables screenEmulation (so getEmulationDescriptions believes no emulation was applied) and the core emulation logic then skips viewport emulation entirely.

2.explanation: The root cause is that DevTools’ entry point (createConfig) forcibly sets settings.screenEmulation.disabled to true so that Lighthouse does not double-apply viewport emulation. But that flag also causes the UI helper getEmulationDescriptions (in core/ui) to report “no emulation.” In addition, the emulate() function in core/lib/emulation.js skips sending any Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride commands when screenEmulation.disabled is true. Although DevTools itself has already applied the viewport settings, the Lighthouse runtime and description logic see the flag and conclude there is no emulation. To fix this, we must adjust createConfig (or downstream description logic) to distinguish DevTools‐applied emulation from a true “disabled” state, and/or update emulate() so that DevTools mode still reports and surfaces the correct mobile emulation in getEmulationDescriptions.
2.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse inside DevTools with a mobile device selected, the Status pane still shows “No emulation with Lighthouse” even though DevTools has indeed applied viewport and user-agent emulation. In the screenshot, DevTools indicates “No emulation” while the audit was run with Slow 4G throttling and device emulation active.
